provenance: Hydra synthetic mass-balance scenarios v1, seed 8317; targets simulated; baseline covariates bootstrapped from attributed real training anchors
limitations: Not a drinking target or daily fluid requirement.
Not clinically validated; unmeasured mass changes remain unresolved.
No dehydration diagnosis or adjustment from HR, HRV, caffeine or creatine.
Synthetic targets; baseline covariates come from deidentified study training anchors. No physiological validation.
Synthetic interval coverage says nothing about real-world accuracy.
Only duration, initial body mass and age enter this model; temperature, humidity and intensity are context only.

sections.title: Hydration-related summary
sections.text: The available record combines logged beverage volume with a separate research exercise-loss estimate. It does not establish total body hydration or a required intake amount.

sections.title: Workout fluid-loss estimate
sections.text: The numerical engine supplies this conditional mass-balance loss proxy and its uncertainty envelope. A planned estimate is separate from an observed loss.

sections.title: Activity context
sections.text: Duration and activity describe the supplied workout. Prior sessions support a projection only when their conditions, protocol and measurement errors meet the numerical engine's comparability checks.

sections.title: Environmental context
sections.text: Supplied temperature and humidity are context. Different or missing conditions can prevent matching; these values do not create an additional numerical loss adjustment.

sections.title: Beverage and electrolyte context
sections.text: Logged beverage volume is separate from documented water content and retention. Electrolyte totals are shown only when every included entry has that documented nutrient; unknown values remain absent.

sections.title: Personal trends
sections.text: Historical logged-day totals describe records, not physiological needs. Days without logs are not measured zero-intake days. Comparable measurements, rather than intake alone, support calibration.

sections.title: Prediction uncertainty
sections.text: Measurement error, incomplete logging and incompatible conditions limit interpretation. More history does not guarantee a narrower range. A historical envelope is not a validated future coverage guarantee.

sections.title: Measurement insights
sections.text: A comparable completed workout with dry before-and-after weighing, recorded consumption and urine, timing and instrument error bounds can improve the evidence available for later predictions. Check mismatched windows and protocols before comparing measurements.

limitations: Research-only exercise loss proxy; not clinically validated or a measure of total body hydration.
Logged intake is an incomplete record; no log does not establish no consumption.
Beverage volume, composition water and physiological retention are different quantities.
A planned forecast is never counted as an already incurred loss.
Exercise accounting omits urine and other losses and is not a full fluid balance or drinking target.
Environmental values describe supplied conditions; no unvalidated weather adjustment is applied.
Heart rate, HRV, caffeine and creatine do not trigger hydration diagnoses or automatic adjustments.
Local sections are deterministic; only a separately labeled saved explanation was generated by Muse Wonder.
Calibration history is retained by the caller; this endpoint does not persist the request or send it to Meta.
